newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sharp denies report on DVD legal action.
newsitem.headline: Sharp denies report on DVD legal action.

text.p: Sharp Corp on Friday denied a newspaper report that it is considering filing complaints with Japan's anti-monopoly watchdog and taking legal measures against companies that developed the digital video disc (DVD).
"We are not considering taking legal action. We did not file complaints and we will not do so," Sharp vice president Atsushi Asada was quoted as saying by a company spokesman.

Business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said in its evening edition on Friday that Sharp thinks because companies that developed DVDs did not unveil standards for the device until late, Sharp has lagged behind in launching DVD products.

DVD is a new recording system which has large storage capacity and is expected to eventually replace videocassette recorders, compact disc (CD) players and CD-ROMs. The system was developed by 10 companies including Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd and Toshiba Corp.
Some of the developers, including Matsushita and Toshiba, announced in August that they would introduce their first DVD products later this year.
Sharp has not yet said when it would launch its DVD products.
